intro: Convert newton meters to foot pounds accurately for automotive lug nuts, engine cylinder heads, and mechanical fasteners. Because 1 pound-foot (ft·lbf) equals 1.355818 N·m under the 1959 international pound and yard standard, 1 N·m equals 0.73756215 lb·ft. Whether you are converting Nm to ft lbs on a European workshop manual or checking newton metres to foot lbs specs on a click torque wrench, this calculator and reference chart compute every value with the exact factor.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Exact NIST Factor & Foot-Pounds vs. Inch-Pounds
items: The exact conversion factor from Newton-meter to Pound-foot (ft·lbf) is 1 ÷ 1.3558179483 (≈ 0.73756215), derived from standard gravity (9.80665 m/s²), 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg, and 1 ft = 0.3048 m.
Never confuse pound-feet (lb·ft) with pound-inches (lb·in): 1 lb·ft equals 12 lb·in, so tightening a small bolt meant for lb·in to a lb·ft setting applies 12× too much torque.

faqs.question: How many pound-feet (lb·ft) are in 1 newton-meter (N·m)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.73756215 pound-feet (lb·ft) in 1 newton-meter (N·m), which rounds to 0.7376 lb·ft for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 pound-foot equals 1.355818 newton-meters.

faqs.question: How do I convert newton-meters to foot-pounds (N·m to lb·ft)?
faqs.answer: Multiply the torque value in newton-meters by 0.73756215 (or divide by 1.355818). For example, 100 N·m × 0.73756215 equals 73.75621 lb·ft.

faqs.question: What is 25 newton-meters in foot-pounds?
faqs.answer: 25 newton-meters (N·m) equals 18.43905 foot-pounds (lb·ft), or roughly 18.4 lb·ft when setting a standard torque wrench.
